packages._note_modules: module_search / module_installed: community modules are the packages named freedomnas-module-<id>; one line per package: name<TAB>version<TAB>description. module_search reads the local package index (update_cache refreshes it).

bootloader._note: FreeBSD boots ZFS-on-root natively -- no UKI/Clover needed. gptzfsboot (BIOS) and loader.efi (UEFI) both understand the same GPT+ZFS layout directly, so one image is bootable both ways without a third-party shim.

be_update: sh -c 'R=$1; pkg -c "$R" which -q /usr/bin/uname >/dev/null 2>&1 && exit 0; set -e; echo "The base system is not installed as packages yet: converting it (pkgbase)"; mkdir -p "$R/usr/local/etc/pkg/repos"; echo "FreeBSD-base: {{ enabled: yes }}" > "$R/usr/local/etc/pkg/repos/FreeBSD-base.conf"; grep -qs "^BACKUP_LIBRARIES" "$R/usr/local/etc/pkg.conf" || echo "BACKUP_LIBRARIES=yes" >> "$R/usr/local/etc/pkg.conf"; S="FreeBSD-set-base FreeBSD-set-kernels"; [ -e "$R/usr/lib32/libc.so.7" ] && S="$S FreeBSD-set-lib32"; [ -e "$R/usr/lib/debug/lib/libc.so.7.debug" ] && S="$S FreeBSD-set-base-dbg"; [ -n "$(ls -A "$R/usr/lib/debug/boot/kernel" 2>/dev/null)" ] && S="$S FreeBSD-set-kernels-dbg"; pkg -c "$R" update -r FreeBSD-base; pkg -c "$R" install -F -y -r FreeBSD-base $S; pkg -c "$R" install --register-only --no-repo-update -y -r FreeBSD-base $S; pkg -c "$R" install -f --no-repo-update -y -r FreeBSD-base $(pkg -c "$R" query -g %n "FreeBSD-*"); chroot "$R" pwd_mkdb -p /etc/master.passwd; chroot "$R" cap_mkdb /etc/login.conf; rm -f "$R/boot/kernel/linker.hints"' pkgbase {root}
updates._be_update_note: The update runs inside a new boot environment mounted at {root}, with pkg chrooted into it: the running system is not touched. The base system comes from the FreeBSD-base repository (pkgbase), so one pkg upgrade updates base and packages together. A system installed from base.txz/kernel.txz is converted the first time, inside the copy, the way pkgbasify does it: the sets matching what is installed are registered without writing files, then installed with -f, so pkg merges the local changes into the configuration files; pwd_mkdb and cap_mkdb rebuild the databases, and linker.hints is regenerated at boot. A copy that does not start takes the system back to the one before.
